rtl_context.user_request: Design an 8 x 8 x 32 GEMM accelerator with signed int8 inputs, int32 wraparound accumulation, per-column int32 bias and ReLU. Use a simple sequential implementation with streaming inputs and outputs and explicit ready/valid handshakes. No optional modes. Fully specify reset and transaction ordering.

design.name: gemm8x8x32_seq_int8_relu_bias
design.description: Sequential fixed-shape GEMM accelerator for C=ReLU(AxB+bias) with int8 inputs and int32 wraparound accumulation.

operations.name: gemm_core
operations.semantics: For one job, compute 8x8 output matrix C where C[i,j]=ReLU(sum_{k=0..31}(A[i,k]*B[k,j]) + bias[j]). A and B elements are signed int8, multiplication is signed, product is sign-extended to int32 before accumulation, accumulation is int32 two's-complement wraparound per add, bias add is int32 wraparound, ReLU outputs 0 when value<0 else value. Fixed dimensions, no optional modes.

data_types.name: int8_s
data_types.conversion_semantics: No conversion on ingress payload; used directly as signed int8.

data_types.name: int32_s
data_types.conversion_semantics: int8*int8 product sign-extended to int32 before add; ReLU compares signed int32.
data_types.overflow_semantics: wraparound modulo 2^32 for accumulator and bias addition

data_objects.name: A_stream
data_objects.role: matrix A elements in row-major order

data_objects.name: B_stream
data_objects.role: matrix B elements in row-major order over KxN

data_objects.name: C_stream
data_objects.role: result matrix elements in row-major order

compute.organization: single-MAC iterative datapath with nested counters
compute.dataflow: load A/B/bias to local buffers, then compute all outputs, then stream outputs
compute.parallelism: 1 multiply-accumulate per cycle during compute phase

storage.name: a_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential during A load; read by address i*K_FIXED+k during compute
storage.port_requirements: 1R/1W logically (single-port time-multiplex acceptable by phase separation)
storage.reuse_semantics: each A element reused across all N outputs of its row during compute
storage.lifetime: from A load completion until compute completion

storage.name: b_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential during B load; read by address k*N_FIXED+j during compute
storage.port_requirements: 1R/1W logically (single-port time-multiplex acceptable by phase separation)
storage.reuse_semantics: each B element reused across all M outputs of its column during compute
storage.lifetime: from B load completion until compute completion

storage.name: bias_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential during bias load; read by index j at start of each output dot-product
storage.reuse_semantics: each bias reused for every row output in its column
storage.lifetime: from bias load completion until compute completion

storage.name: c_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential per computed output; read sequential for output streaming
storage.reuse_semantics: temporary retention between compute and output phases
storage.lifetime: from first computed output until final output handshake

pipeline.responsibility: accept command then A/B/bias streams via ready/valid into local buffers
pipeline.valid_behavior: input transfers occur only on ready&&valid
pipeline.stall_behavior: when not ready, sender must hold valid/payload stable; DUT state unchanged

pipeline.responsibility: iterative MAC, bias add, ReLU, store C element
pipeline.valid_behavior: internal step each cycle when not reset
pipeline.stall_behavior: no external backpressure in compute; stage runs until done or reset

pipeline.valid_behavior: output transfer occurs only on ready&&valid
pipeline.stall_behavior: hold out_valid and payload stable while out_ready=0

control.strategy: single FSM controlling phase progression IDLE->LOAD_A->LOAD_B->LOAD_BIAS->COMPUTE->OUTPUT->DONE->IDLE; DONE is exactly one cycle
control.state_progression: advance only when phase transfer/count complete; compute advances per cycle by counters i,j,k; DONE lasts exactly one cycle, with all input ready outputs low during DONE, and transition to IDLE occurs on the next cycle where cmd_ready may reassert
control.error_behavior: Protocol violation is evaluated only on attempted transfer events (ready&&valid), not on valid-only observation while ready=0. Error pulses for one cycle when: (a) cmd transfer occurs with cmd_payload!=1, or (b) any input transfer occurs on a channel whose phase is inactive, or (c) a command transfer occurs while not IDLE. In all cases the illegal transfer is ignored for state/count progression and FSM remains in current legal state.
control.error_recovery: automatic recovery by remaining in current legal state; next legal handshake proceeds without reset

reset.required_state: FSM=IDLE, busy=0, completion=0, error=0, all channel ready outputs low (cmd_ready=0, a_ready=0, b_ready=0, bias_ready=0), valid outputs=0, counters/pointers reset to 0, internal partial-job data treated invalid

architecture_contract.latency_model: Variable due to ready/valid stalls. Stall-free legal job timing uses cycle count from first cycle after accepted final bias beat to compute_done pulse inclusive with 1-cycle synchronous operand reads: per output element, 1 bias-read issue cycle + 1 bias-capture/init cycle + K_FIXED MAC iterations each with (1 address-issue cycle + 1 MAC-update cycle) + 1 finalize/write cycle = (2*K_FIXED + 3) cycles; total compute cycles = M_FIXED*N_FIXED*(2*K_FIXED + 3) = 4288 at defaults. Full stall-free job latency components: 1 cmd beat +256 A beats +256 B beats +8 bias beats +4288 compute cycles +64 output beats +1 completion pulse cycle. Reset aborts in-flight job and no completion for aborted job.
architectural_invariants: Exactly one job in flight; no overlap or queueing.
Accepted command snapshots fixed dimensions implicitly (8,8,32).
No operand transfer accepted outside its designated phase.
Output order is strict row-major C[0,0]..C[7,7].
Each accepted legal job produces exactly 64 output transfers and one completion pulse.
ready/valid transfer rule is globally ready&&valid; payload stability required under stall.
open_assumptions: Command payload is 1-bit start token with value 1 as only legal encoding.
Host presents A then B then bias sections; no interleaving.
Illegal transfers are physically representable and reported by one-cycle error pulse.

channels.name: cmd_ch
channels.backpressure: cmd_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0. On the first rising clk edge with rst_n=1, if FSM state is IDLE then cmd_ready shall be high in that same cycle and a held cmd_valid/cmd_payload may transfer on that edge (ready&&valid).

channels.name: a_ch
channels.ordering: row-major A[i,k] with i outer, k inner
channels.backpressure: a_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, a_ready is high only in LOAD_A.

channels.name: b_ch
channels.ordering: row-major over KxN: B[k,j] with k outer, j inner
channels.backpressure: b_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, b_ready is high only in LOAD_B.

channels.name: bias_ch
channels.backpressure: bias_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, bias_ready is high only in LOAD_BIAS.

channels.name: out_ch
channels.framing: 64 beats per job with out_last=1 only on final beat
channels.ordering: row-major C[i,j] with i outer, j inner
channels.backpressure: producer holds valid/payload/last stable until out_ready

signals.name: rst_n
signals.semantic: active-low synchronous reset; when low, no channel transfer is accepted or emitted

signals.name: cmd_ready
signals.semantic: high only in IDLE when rst_n=1 and ready for new command

signals.name: cmd_payload
signals.semantic: must be 1 for legal start command

signals.name: busy
signals.semantic: busy=1 from the cycle of accepted legal command transfer through and including the cycle of the final accepted output transfer (final out_hs, out_last=1). busy deasserts in the immediately following cycle. completion pulses high for exactly that same following cycle (one-cycle pulse), then returns low.

signals.name: completion
signals.semantic: one-cycle pulse in DONE state immediately after the cycle of final output transfer handshake

signals.name: error
signals.semantic: one-cycle pulse on illegal command encoding or illegal phase transfer attempt

global_handshake_rules.transfer_condition: A channel transfer occurs iff ready && valid sampled high on rising clk and rst_n=1.
global_handshake_rules.stall_behavior: For every ready/valid channel, in every cycle with valid=1 and ready=0 and rst_n=1, the producer shall hold payload/metadata/last stable. Producer may keep valid asserted across arbitrary stall duration and may deassert valid before transfer; if it remains asserted, associated payload/metadata/last must remain unchanged until a transfer occurs or valid is deasserted. When rst_n=0, DUT outputs may synchronously drop to reset values and any pending non-transferred beat is aborted.

modules.name: gemm8x8x32_top
modules.responsibility: external interface binding and integration of control, buffers, compute, and output stream

modules.name: gemm_ctrl_fsm
modules.responsibility: phase FSM, counters, handshake qualification, busy/completion/error generation

modules.name: operand_buffer_bank
modules.responsibility: store A/B/bias/C arrays; provide compute read ports and output read port

ports.name: rdata_a
ports.semantics: A read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

ports.name: rdata_b
ports.semantics: B read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

ports.name: rdata_bias
ports.semantics: bias read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

ports.name: rdata_c
ports.semantics: C read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

modules.name: mac_sequencer
modules.responsibility: generate i/j/k traversal, perform signed MAC with wrap, bias add, ReLU, and write C

ports.name: we_c
ports.semantics: C write enable pulse when one output finalized

modules.name: output_streamer
modules.responsibility: read C buffer and emit out_valid/out_payload/out_last under backpressure

functional: Given one legal command and exact required operand counts, output equals software oracle C=ReLU(AxB+bias) with int32 wraparound on accumulation and bias add.
A stream acceptance order must be exactly 256 row-major A beats, then 256 row-major B beats, then 8 bias beats; early/late wrong-channel valid causes error pulse and no phase advance.
Output stream emits exactly 64 beats row-major; out_last asserted only on beat 64.
K recurrence correctness: accumulator initialized to 0, updated exactly for k=0..31 once each; K=32 fixed case no double count.
Completion pulses exactly once after final output handshake of a legal job; no completion for reset-aborted job.

Mandatory stall-free latency check: for a legal job with no channel stalls (all required valids and readies asserted whenever applicable), total cycles from accepted cmd transfer cycle to completion pulse cycle inclusive shall equal 4874 at defaults (1 cmd + 256 A + 256 B + 8 bias + 4288 compute + 64 output + 1 completion), and compute phase cycles from first cycle after accepted final bias beat to compute_done pulse inclusive shall equal 4288.
verification: Minimum 100 randomized legal jobs with random int8 A/B and int32 bias, randomized out_ready and randomized input valid stalls.
Reset tests: reset in IDLE, during each load phase, during compute, and during output; verify abort semantics and no ghost outputs.
Backpressure tests on all ready/valid channels: payload/last stability while stalled and correct resume edge.

Illegal behavior tests: cmd_payload=0 when cmd handshake, command valid while busy, and wrong input channel ready&&valid transfer in non-owning phase each produce one-cycle error and recover to continue legal operation. Valid asserted alone while ready=0 in a non-owning phase is legal backpressure observation and must not error.
Ordering test for pending next command while busy: cmd_ready low; source may hold cmd_valid high; acceptance occurs on first cycle returning to IDLE with cmd_ready high and valid high.
rtl: RTL must be synthesizable SystemVerilog only; no real/shortreal/delay/class/force-release constructs.
Single clock synchronous design with active-low synchronous reset behavior matching contract.
No combinational loops on ready/valid paths; registered control state and counters.
All declared top-level and inter-module ports implemented with matching widths/sign semantics and 1-cycle memory read latency assumptions honored.
fpga_handoff: Provide Vivado synthesis/implementation reports only from deterministic tool runs after verification passes.
Do not estimate or fabricate Fmax/area/power/utilization; report only tool-produced metrics.
Handoff must include exact RTL commit hash and constraint files used for deterministic reproduction.

verifier_result.summary: Frozen artifacts do not define a complete externally observable contract for illegal wrong-channel 'valid in non-owning phase' when ready=0 versus ready=1 gating needed to build a single deterministic oracle/checker for mandated illegal tests and phase-consumption assertions.

architecture_conflict.issue: Acceptance criteria require 'wrong input channel valid in non-owning phase each produce one-cycle error'. Architecture error_behavior says illegal phase error is evaluated only on attempted transfer events (ready&&valid), and when not in owning phase that channel ready is specified low. These statements imply valid-only while ready=0 should not error, conflicting with required illegal test expectation if interpreted as valid assertion alone.
architecture_conflict.evidence: (1) architecture.control.error_behavior: error only on attempted transfer events (ready&&valid). (2) interface backpressure per channel: ready high only in owning phase, thus wrong-channel ready=0 outside phase. (3) acceptance_criteria.verification explicitly demands wrong-channel valid in non-owning phase produce error pulse.
architecture_conflict.requested_architect_decision: Clarify whether illegal wrong-channel condition is (A) valid&&ready attempted transfer only, or (B) valid assertion in forbidden phase regardless of ready. If (A), define required stimulus form to make it representable; if (B), amend transfer-rule exception explicitly.

known_verification_gaps: Executable TB/oracle generation blocked pending single interpretation of illegal wrong-channel error trigger.

findings.issue: Reset behavior conflicts: reset.required_state says cmd_ready=1 in IDLE during reset, while rst_n semantic says when low no channel transfer is accepted or emitted. This is ambiguous for whether cmd_ready must be high or low under reset.
findings.requested_change: Define reset handshake outputs unambiguously in both artifacts (e.g., while rst_n=0 force all ready/valid low including cmd_ready, or explicitly allow cmd_ready=1 but state no transfer can occur because reset gates acceptance). Ensure both sections match exactly.

findings.issue: Stall-free compute latency is specified as 2112 cycles (=64*32 MAC +64 finalize), but operand_buffer_bank declares 1-cycle synchronous read latency for A/B/bias, which typically requires explicit prefetch/pipeline bubbles or overlapped scheduling. Current contract does not provide cycle-accurate rule reconciling these, so independent implementations may disagree on timing/compute_done assertion.
findings.requested_change: Add explicit compute micro-schedule consistent with 1-cycle sync reads (address issue timing, when MAC update occurs, when bias is read/applied, and exact condition for compute_done). Either adjust the 2112-cycle figure or specify overlap rules that make it achievable.

findings.issue: "protocol violation if input valid arrives on wrong stream phase" conflicts with ready/valid semantics elsewhere: with ready low, valid alone is normally non-accepted and legal. As written, implementations may pulse error on any asserted valid while not in phase, even without transfer intent.
findings.requested_change: Define illegal wrong-phase condition explicitly in signal terms (e.g., whether error is triggered by valid-only observation, by attempted transfer, or by a specific phase/ready qualification) and make it consistent with global handshake rules.

findings.issue: Rule allows payload/metadata/last stability requirement to end when valid drops before transfer ("until transfer or valid drops"), which can conflict with stricter ready/valid verification expectations and produce non-deterministic producer behavior under prolonged stall.
findings.requested_change: Tighten rule to require payload/metadata/last stability for every cycle valid=1 and ready=0, and clarify whether producer is permitted to deassert valid before eventual transfer on each channel.

findings.issue: Reset requires all ready outputs low, while interface channel backpressure text defines readiness by phase only and does not restate reset precedence per channel. This can cause mismatched assertions at boundaries.
findings.requested_change: Add explicit per-channel statement (or global precedence rule) that reset forces cmd_ready/a_ready/b_ready/bias_ready low regardless of phase logic, and that no input transfer is accepted when rst_n=0.

findings.issue: "busy ... deasserts before completion pulse cycle" is timing-specific but not tied to a precise cycle relation with DONE state entry and completion pulse generation; different implementations may differ by one cycle while still appearing compliant elsewhere.
findings.requested_change: Specify exact cycle relationship between final out_hs, busy deassertion, and completion pulse (e.g., busy drops in cycle T+1 and completion pulses in same/next defined cycle).

findings.issue: Compute-cycle formula is precise, but acceptance criteria do not bind it as a normative latency requirement; implementers may alter internal micro-sequencing and still pass functional checks, creating contract drift.
findings.requested_change: State whether the provided compute cycle model (2*K+3 per output, 4288 total at defaults) is mandatory or informative. If mandatory, add an acceptance criterion that checks exact cycle count under stall-free conditions.

findings.issue: Spec says cmd_ready is high only in IDLE when rst_n=1, while reset.required_state says all ready outputs low and does not explicitly define first-cycle behavior on reset deassertion. This can cause disagreement on whether a held cmd_valid/cmd_payload may handshake on the first cycle rst_n rises if FSM is already IDLE.
findings.requested_change: Add an explicit executable rule for reset-release handshake timing (e.g., whether cmd_ready may assert immediately on first rst_n=1 cycle in IDLE, and whether command can be accepted that same cycle).

findings.issue: FSM sequence includes DONE->IDLE, while busy/completion semantics define completion pulse in the cycle after final output handshake and busy deassert in that same following cycle. The contract does not explicitly state whether DONE is exactly one cycle and whether any ready signal may assert during DONE. This can create implementation variance in command acceptance timing around completion.
findings.requested_change: Specify DONE state duration and readiness behavior explicitly (e.g., DONE is exactly one cycle, all input ready signals low in DONE, cmd_ready reasserts only upon entry to IDLE on next cycle).

findings.issue: Rule says illegal transfer is ignored for state/count progression and FSM remains in current legal state, but does not explicitly state whether illegally transferred payload is written into operand buffers or other data-path state.
findings.requested_change: Add an explicit no-side-effect rule: any illegal transfer pulse must not write/update A/B/bias/C buffers, counters, accumulators, output registers, or phase state (only one-cycle error pulse may occur).

(2) interface backpressure per channel: ready high only in owning phase, thus wrong-channel ready=0 outside phase. (3) acceptance_criteria.verification explicitly demands wrong-channel valid in non-owning phase produce error pulse.
architecture_conflict.requested_architect_decision: Clarify whether illegal wrong-channel condition is (A) valid&&ready attempted transfer only, or (B) valid assertion in forbidden phase regardless of ready. If (A), define required stimulus form to make it representable; if (B), amend transfer-rule exception explicitly.

verification_context.user_request: Design an 8 x 8 x 32 GEMM accelerator with signed int8 inputs, int32 wraparound accumulation, per-column int32 bias and ReLU. Use a simple sequential implementation with streaming inputs and outputs and explicit ready/valid handshakes. No optional modes. Fully specify reset and transaction ordering.

design.name: gemm8x8x32_seq_int8_relu_bias
design.description: Sequential fixed-shape GEMM accelerator for C=ReLU(AxB+bias) with int8 inputs and int32 wraparound accumulation.

operations.name: gemm_core
operations.semantics: For one job, compute 8x8 output matrix C where C[i,j]=ReLU(sum_{k=0..31}(A[i,k]*B[k,j]) + bias[j]). A and B elements are signed int8, multiplication is signed, product is sign-extended to int32 before accumulation, accumulation is int32 two's-complement wraparound per add, bias add is int32 wraparound, ReLU outputs 0 when value<0 else value. Fixed dimensions, no optional modes.

data_types.name: int8_s
data_types.conversion_semantics: No conversion on ingress payload; used directly as signed int8.

data_types.name: int32_s
data_types.conversion_semantics: int8*int8 product sign-extended to int32 before add; ReLU compares signed int32.
data_types.overflow_semantics: wraparound modulo 2^32 for accumulator and bias addition

data_objects.name: A_stream
data_objects.role: matrix A elements in row-major order

data_objects.name: B_stream
data_objects.role: matrix B elements in row-major order over KxN

data_objects.name: C_stream
data_objects.role: result matrix elements in row-major order

compute.organization: single-MAC iterative datapath with nested counters
compute.dataflow: load A/B/bias to local buffers, then compute all outputs, then stream outputs
compute.parallelism: 1 multiply-accumulate per cycle during compute phase

storage.name: a_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential during A load; read by address i*K_FIXED+k during compute
storage.port_requirements: 1R/1W logically (single-port time-multiplex acceptable by phase separation)
storage.reuse_semantics: each A element reused across all N outputs of its row during compute
storage.lifetime: from A load completion until compute completion

storage.name: b_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential during B load; read by address k*N_FIXED+j during compute
storage.port_requirements: 1R/1W logically (single-port time-multiplex acceptable by phase separation)
storage.reuse_semantics: each B element reused across all M outputs of its column during compute
storage.lifetime: from B load completion until compute completion

storage.name: bias_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential during bias load; read by index j at start of each output dot-product
storage.reuse_semantics: each bias reused for every row output in its column
storage.lifetime: from bias load completion until compute completion

storage.name: c_buf
storage.access_pattern: write sequential per computed output; read sequential for output streaming
storage.reuse_semantics: temporary retention between compute and output phases
storage.lifetime: from first computed output until final output handshake

pipeline.responsibility: accept command then A/B/bias streams via ready/valid into local buffers
pipeline.valid_behavior: input transfers occur only on ready&&valid
pipeline.stall_behavior: when not ready, sender must hold valid/payload stable; DUT state unchanged

pipeline.responsibility: iterative MAC, bias add, ReLU, store C element
pipeline.valid_behavior: internal step each cycle when not reset
pipeline.stall_behavior: no external backpressure in compute; stage runs until done or reset

pipeline.valid_behavior: output transfer occurs only on ready&&valid
pipeline.stall_behavior: hold out_valid and payload stable while out_ready=0

control.state_progression: advance only when phase transfer/count complete; compute advances per cycle by counters i,j,k
control.error_behavior: Protocol violation is evaluated only on attempted transfer events (ready&&valid), not on valid-only observation while ready=0. Error pulses for one cycle when: (a) cmd transfer occurs with cmd_payload!=1, or (b) any input transfer occurs on a channel whose phase is inactive, or (c) a command transfer occurs while not IDLE. In all cases the illegal transfer is ignored for state/count progression and FSM remains in current legal state.
control.error_recovery: automatic recovery by remaining in current legal state; next legal handshake proceeds without reset

reset.required_state: FSM=IDLE, busy=0, completion=0, error=0, all channel ready outputs low (cmd_ready=0, a_ready=0, b_ready=0, bias_ready=0), valid outputs=0, counters/pointers reset to 0, internal partial-job data treated invalid

architecture_contract.latency_model: Variable due to ready/valid stalls. Stall-free legal job timing uses cycle count from first cycle after accepted final bias beat to compute_done pulse inclusive with 1-cycle synchronous operand reads: per output element, 1 bias-read issue cycle + 1 bias-capture/init cycle + K_FIXED MAC iterations each with (1 address-issue cycle + 1 MAC-update cycle) + 1 finalize/write cycle = (2*K_FIXED + 3) cycles; total compute cycles = M_FIXED*N_FIXED*(2*K_FIXED + 3) = 4288 at defaults. Full stall-free job latency components: 1 cmd beat +256 A beats +256 B beats +8 bias beats +4288 compute cycles +64 output beats +1 completion pulse cycle. Reset aborts in-flight job and no completion for aborted job.
architectural_invariants: Exactly one job in flight; no overlap or queueing.
Accepted command snapshots fixed dimensions implicitly (8,8,32).
No operand transfer accepted outside its designated phase.
Output order is strict row-major C[0,0]..C[7,7].
Each accepted legal job produces exactly 64 output transfers and one completion pulse.
ready/valid transfer rule is globally ready&&valid; payload stability required under stall.
open_assumptions: Command payload is 1-bit start token with value 1 as only legal encoding.
Host presents A then B then bias sections; no interleaving.
Illegal transfers are physically representable and reported by one-cycle error pulse.

channels.name: cmd_ch
channels.backpressure: cmd_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, cmd_ready is high only in IDLE.

channels.name: a_ch
channels.ordering: row-major A[i,k] with i outer, k inner
channels.backpressure: a_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, a_ready is high only in LOAD_A.

channels.name: b_ch
channels.ordering: row-major over KxN: B[k,j] with k outer, j inner
channels.backpressure: b_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, b_ready is high only in LOAD_B.

channels.name: bias_ch
channels.backpressure: bias_ready is forced low whenever rst_n=0; when rst_n=1, bias_ready is high only in LOAD_BIAS.

channels.name: out_ch
channels.framing: 64 beats per job with out_last=1 only on final beat
channels.ordering: row-major C[i,j] with i outer, j inner
channels.backpressure: producer holds valid/payload/last stable until out_ready

signals.name: rst_n
signals.semantic: active-low synchronous reset; when low, no channel transfer is accepted or emitted

signals.name: cmd_ready
signals.semantic: high only in IDLE when rst_n=1 and ready for new command

signals.name: cmd_payload
signals.semantic: must be 1 for legal start command

signals.name: busy
signals.semantic: busy=1 from the cycle of accepted legal command transfer through and including the cycle of the final accepted output transfer (final out_hs, out_last=1). busy deasserts in the immediately following cycle. completion pulses high for exactly that same following cycle (one-cycle pulse), then returns low.

signals.name: completion
signals.semantic: one-cycle pulse in DONE state after final output transfer handshake

signals.name: error
signals.semantic: one-cycle pulse on illegal command encoding or illegal phase transfer attempt

global_handshake_rules.transfer_condition: A channel transfer occurs iff ready && valid sampled high on rising clk and rst_n=1.
global_handshake_rules.stall_behavior: For every ready/valid channel, in every cycle with valid=1 and ready=0 and rst_n=1, the producer shall hold payload/metadata/last stable. Producer may keep valid asserted across arbitrary stall duration and may deassert valid before transfer; if it remains asserted, associated payload/metadata/last must remain unchanged until a transfer occurs or valid is deasserted. When rst_n=0, DUT outputs may synchronously drop to reset values and any pending non-transferred beat is aborted.

modules.name: gemm8x8x32_top
modules.responsibility: external interface binding and integration of control, buffers, compute, and output stream

modules.name: gemm_ctrl_fsm
modules.responsibility: phase FSM, counters, handshake qualification, busy/completion/error generation

modules.name: operand_buffer_bank
modules.responsibility: store A/B/bias/C arrays; provide compute read ports and output read port

ports.name: rdata_a
ports.semantics: A read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

ports.name: rdata_b
ports.semantics: B read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

ports.name: rdata_bias
ports.semantics: bias read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

ports.name: rdata_c
ports.semantics: C read data, 1-cycle sync read latency

modules.name: mac_sequencer
modules.responsibility: generate i/j/k traversal, perform signed MAC with wrap, bias add, ReLU, and write C

ports.name: we_c
ports.semantics: C write enable pulse when one output finalized

modules.name: output_streamer
modules.responsibility: read C buffer and emit out_valid/out_payload/out_last under backpressure

functional: Given one legal command and exact required operand counts, output equals software oracle C=ReLU(AxB+bias) with int32 wraparound on accumulation and bias add.
A stream acceptance order must be exactly 256 row-major A beats, then 256 row-major B beats, then 8 bias beats; early/late wrong-channel valid causes error pulse and no phase advance.
Output stream emits exactly 64 beats row-major; out_last asserted only on beat 64.
K recurrence correctness: accumulator initialized to 0, updated exactly for k=0..31 once each; K=32 fixed case no double count.
Completion pulses exactly once after final output handshake of a legal job; no completion for reset-aborted job.

Mandatory stall-free latency check: for a legal job with no channel stalls (all required valids and readies asserted whenever applicable), total cycles from accepted cmd transfer cycle to completion pulse cycle inclusive shall equal 4874 at defaults (1 cmd + 256 A + 256 B + 8 bias + 4288 compute + 64 output + 1 completion), and compute phase cycles from first cycle after accepted final bias beat to compute_done pulse inclusive shall equal 4288.
verification: Minimum 100 randomized legal jobs with random int8 A/B and int32 bias, randomized out_ready and randomized input valid stalls.
Reset tests: reset in IDLE, during each load phase, during compute, and during output; verify abort semantics and no ghost outputs.
Backpressure tests on all ready/valid channels: payload/last stability while stalled and correct resume edge.

Illegal behavior tests: cmd_payload=0 when cmd handshake, command valid while busy, and wrong input channel valid in non-owning phase each produce one-cycle error and recover to continue legal operation.
Ordering test for pending next command while busy: cmd_ready low; source may hold cmd_valid high; acceptance occurs on first cycle returning to IDLE with cmd_ready high and valid high.
rtl: RTL must be synthesizable SystemVerilog only; no real/shortreal/delay/class/force-release constructs.
Single clock synchronous design with active-low synchronous reset behavior matching contract.
No combinational loops on ready/valid paths; registered control state and counters.
All declared top-level and inter-module ports implemented with matching widths/sign semantics and 1-cycle memory read latency assumptions honored.
fpga_handoff: Provide Vivado synthesis/implementation reports only from deterministic tool runs after verification passes.
Do not estimate or fabricate Fmax/area/power/utilization; report only tool-produced metrics.
Handoff must include exact RTL commit hash and constraint files used for deterministic reproduction.

limitations: Generated oracle and tests undergo deterministic structural checks and simulation; this is not a proof of oracle correctness.
Vivado adapter requires validation against the installed Vivado version and FPGA target.
Out-of-context PPA excludes board I/O integration; power is a tool estimate and maximum frequency is not measured.
